item.description:
Scrabble Frenzy has 60 letter tiles, 45 word cards with partially-spelled words (e.g. ---ING, SP---, -EA-), and 10 Power Up cards that give benefits to players (e.g. Letter Swipe, Double Word Score).
At the start of a round the 60 letter tiles are divided face down among the players, and one word card is revealed for each player, plus one extra. Then players turn up their letters, and simultaneously try to fill out the cards with them. When they can they call out the word(s) for a card, claim it, and place the letters on the card; their remaining letter tiles can be used on other tiles. At the end of a round, each card with optional bonus spaces filled out earns the player a Power Up card that can give them abilities for a following round.
After six rounds, players total the points, and the highest total wins.

item.description:
The LCD shows the word that players need to find out, and clues are given, while the time to respond is counted. The device is passed from hand to hand with the correct answers.
Two game modes: individual or team. Individual has the option for easy or difficult (so there is really 3 modes). After choosing the options, start the game.
Individual mode: The first question appears on the screen. For example: words beginning with "A" and containing the letter "N". From that time it begins to count time (which leads the device). The player with the device in hand says a word with those conditions, and if you do, the device passes to the next player quickly, which should be another word that has not been said already. When the time expires, an alarm sounds and the player with the device on hand at the time (in this moment), is eliminated. New question appears on the screen, repeating the same cycle with the players that are left. The goal is not to be eliminated, as when only one player is the winner.
Team play is quite different. The question appears on the screen, and each of the teams will discuss among its members the number of words that are able to say with those conditions, in 60 seconds. It's like an auction. The team that makes the best bet, will play the first round of 60 sec. and each of the team members will be saying a word and pressed his team number on the device (1 or 2) so that it takes account at the end of 60 seconds. If successful you will get the first point, otherwise, the point is for the other team. Then comes another round of 60 seconds. with new question and following the same mechanics.
When starting the game will have agreed how many rounds will be played or how long the game. Once completed, the device itself will tell how many points each team leads, and whoever has the most points is the winner.

Letter tiles are played twice per turn, and must be used from the beginning of each word and sequentially toward the end. All tiles are face up once held by a player. item.description:
Fundamentally, Scrabble Overturn is a scoring variant on Scrabble (q.v.)
The board is a simple grid, into which one places "letter cylinders" which depict a given letter in four colors. If a player employs existing cylinders in making a word, those cylinders are rotated to show the active player's color.
Words are scored as played if they score a minimum of 12 points (otherwise zero points) with a bonus for playing all seven cylinders in one turn. A final end-game score is added to individual player scores, but only for words that are all of one color. Multi-color words may be broken down into segments and scored if they are also valid words.

item.description: Each player is dealt four cards and must have only four cards in his or her hand at the end of each turn. The remaining cards form a "pick-up" pile with the top card turned over to form the beginning of a "put-down" pile. A player selects a card from either of the two piles and discards a card onto the "put-down" pile. Sir Scrabble and Muddler cards cannot be taken. A Sir Scrabble card can be discarded to take another turn. Conversely, a Muddler card can be discarded so that the next player will have to lose a turn. The "put-down" pile should be turned over, if all of the cards from the "pick-up" pile have been used. The winner is one who collects four cards of any of the following: queen, jeweler, baby, librarian, waiter, or zookeeper.
